precepts.text: Hannah vowed a vow: give unto thine handmaid a man child, and I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life; the pattern of a singular vow.
precepts.point: Christ taught on this because a vow is dangerous: you must pay your vow. Better not to swear at all, but let your communication be yea, yea; that is why we just say Lord's will, Lord's will I get this done.

note.label: Leviticus 27: Vows and Estimations

precepts.why:
Hannah is the pattern of a singular vow. A singular vow is a man binding himself to the Most High: promising that in exchange for a blessing he will give himself, or what is his, to the service of the Lord.

Hannah “was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the Lord, and wept sore. And she vowed a vow, and said, O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.”

The blessing asked was a man child; the thing vowed was the child himself, a person given for the Lord, as Leviticus 27 speaks of the persons being for the Lord. That is how the story of Samuel began.

precepts.text: All the days of the vow of his separation no rasor comes upon his head; he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.
precepts.point: She vowed a vow: O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no rasor come upon his head. What law is that going back to? The law of the Nazarite. Put some things together as you read through Samuel about Samuel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“All the days of the vow of his separation there shall no razor come upon his head: until the days be fulfilled, in the which he separateth himself unto the Lord, he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.”

Hannah, in bitterness of soul, vowed: if the Lord would “give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.” What law is that going back to? The law of the Nazarite. Put that together as you read through Samuel about Samuel: he was given to the Lord under the Nazarite vow.

The locks of a Nazarite are hair braided so that it locks into place as it grows long. When you braid your hair, you are locking it in.

precepts.text: Samson spoke of the seven locks of his head; the locks of the Nazarite vow.
precepts.point: The locks of a Nazarite are hair braided so that it locks into place as it grows long; when you braid your hair you are locking it in. You read of the locks of Samson's hair back in the book of Judges; Samson was under that same vow.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“And Delilah said unto Samson, Hitherto thou hast mocked me, and told me lies: tell me wherewith thou mightest be bound. And he said unto her, If thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web.”

Samson spoke of the seven locks of his head: the locks of the Nazarite vow. Samson was under that same vow that Hannah made for Samuel, that there should no razor come upon his head. The locks are the hair of the head let grow and locked in, as the law of the Nazarite says.

precepts.text: This is the confidence that we have in him: if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us, and we have the petitions that we desired of him.
precepts.point: Why did the Lord grant her petition? It was the will of the Most High for Samuel to come through Hannah; it was just in his time. And she was granted it because of what she did before she even asked: she kept his commandments and did those things that are pleasing in his sight.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.”

Hannah poured out her soul before the Lord, speaking in her heart so that only her lips moved, and Eli took her for drunken. When she told him, “I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord”, Eli answered, “Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.” She believed when she heard the word of Eli: she “went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.”

Why did the Lord grant her petition? It was the will of the Most High for Samuel to come through Hannah; it was just in his time.

Understand this: a lot of us pray for things that the Lord has not given to us. The Most High has the infinite and ultimate wisdom and knows what is best for us, so some things he keeps back from us, and we have to accept that and know that. If it be his will, we receive what we ask, in his time; if it is not his will, we will not receive it.

precepts.text: Whatsoever we ask, we receive of him, because we keep his commandments, and do those things that are pleasing in his sight.
precepts.point: Why did the Lord grant her petition? It was the will of the Most High for Samuel to come through Hannah; it was just in his time. And she was granted it because of what she did before she even asked: she kept his commandments and did those things that are pleasing in his sight.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“And whatsoever we ask, we receive of him, because we keep his commandments, and do those things that are pleasing in his sight.”

Hannah was granted her petition because of what she did before she even asked: she kept his commandments and did those things that are pleasing in his sight. She went up to Shiloh and prayed before the Lord, and Eli said, “the God of Israel grant thee thy petition”.

If we keep the commandments and it be his will, we receive whatsoever we ask, in his time.

precepts.text: Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord: in the feast of unleavened bread, which is known as Passover; in the feast of weeks, which is known as Pentecost; and in the feast of tabernacles, which is also known as the feast of booths. Elkanah, who lived in mount Ephraim, was applying this law over and over again.
precepts.point: The man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto the Lord the yearly sacrifice, and his vow. What is that yearly sacrifice going into? Deuteronomy 16:16.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles: and they shall not appear before the Lord empty”.

The feast of unleavened bread is known as Passover; the feast of weeks is known as Pentecost; and the feast of tabernacles is also known as the feast of booths.

That is what the yearly sacrifice is going into when “the man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto the Lord the yearly sacrifice, and his vow.” Elkanah, who lived in mount Ephraim, was applying this law over and over again, going up to the place the Lord had chosen.

precepts.text: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay. The angel before whom you must not say it was an error is your personal angel, your guardian angel for lack of a better word, that watches over you and listens to you; do not say, I did not mean to say that. Yes you did; the angel recorded it and knew exactly what it was.
precepts.point: She said to Eli, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the Lord. For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. That is great faith right there that Hannah had, and she kept her promise: Hannah was an upright and honest woman.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.”

“Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error”. The angel is your personal angel, your guardian angel for lack of a better word, that watches over you and listens to you. Do not say, I did not mean to say that. Yes you did; the angel recorded it and knew exactly what it was.

Hannah paid her vow. When she had weaned the child she brought him to the house of the Lord in Shiloh and said, “For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: Therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord.” That is great faith right there, and she kept her promise. Hannah was an upright and honest woman.

precepts.text: That is why Christ went on to say, Let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay. Whatever comes out of your mouth, be upright and honest, and do that which comes out of thy mouth.
precepts.point: She said to Eli, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the Lord. For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. That is great faith right there that Hannah had, and she kept her promise: Hannah was an upright and honest woman.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
That is why Christ went on to say, “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

Whatever comes out of your mouth, be upright and honest, and do that which comes out of thy mouth. Hannah said she would give the child to the Lord all the days of his life, and she did: “as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord.” Her yea was yea.

So the high priest Eli had two sons named Hophni and Phinehas. Watch this.

points: There was a certain man of mount Ephraim named Elkanah, and he had two wives: the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: Elkanah went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the Lord of hosts in Shiloh, where the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the Lord, were. Shiloh is another name for Jerusalem.

points: When Elkanah offered, he gave to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters portions; but unto Hannah he gave a worthy portion, for he loved Hannah: but the Lord had shut up her womb.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: Her adversary provoked her sore, to make her fret, because the Lord had shut up her womb; year by year, when she went up to the house of the Lord, she provoked her, so that Hannah wept and did not eat. The women of Israel have not changed one bit: even back in the times of Samuel there was a sister vexing a barren woman and rubbing it in her face. Sisters of Israel have to get their spirits right; no doubt about it, you are Israel.
